panels.title: Initial copy (overall)
panels.description: How much of the initial copy is done, worked out by replicare the same way as the ETA: each table counts for its size on the source, and tables linked in a loop count their link-filling pass too. It stays under 100% until every table has finished and switched to streaming.

panels.title: Initial copy ETA
panels.description: How long the initial copy has left, worked out by replicare from how much is still to copy and how fast it went over the last 10 minutes. Each table counts for its size on the source, so a table of large rows isn't made to look quick by a run of small ones. 'Not moving' means nothing was copied in the last 10 minutes. The sizes and row counts are the source's own estimates and the link-filling pass for tables linked in a loop isn't included, so treat it as a guide.

panels.title: Tables still copying
panels.description: Tables in the initial-copy phase. Reaches 0 when every table is streaming.

panels.title: Tables streaming
panels.description: Tables that finished their initial copy and are replicating changes.

panels.title: Copy rate (rows/s)
panels.description: Rows per second being copied right now (all tables).

panels.title: Initial copy progress % (per table)
panels.description: 100 * rows_copied / rows_target. Reaches 100% when a table finishes its initial copy.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (table) (replicare_rows_copied_total{sync=~"$sync", table=~"$table"}) / clamp_min(sum by (table) (replicare_initial_copy_rows_target{sync=~"$sync", table=~"$table"}), 1)

panels.title: Rows copied vs target (per table)
panels.description: Absolute initial-copy progress.

panels.title: Link-filling pass (per table)
panels.description: Tables linked in a loop of foreign keys are copied in two stages: the rows go in with the links between them left empty, then this pass fills the links in. Each bar is how far that pass has got for one table. A bar appears once its table's pass is planned and fills as it runs.

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (table) (replicare_link_fill_rows_total{sync=~"$sync", table=~"$table"}) or 0 * sum by (table) (replicare_link_fill_rows_target{sync=~"$sync", table=~"$table"})) / clamp_min(sum by (table) (replicare_link_fill_rows_target{sync=~"$sync", table=~"$table"}), 1)

panels.title: Indexes built again
panels.description: Plain target indexes replicare took down for the initial copy, and how many are built again. They are built once every table is streaming, one at a time, without blocking writes. Empty when no indexes were taken down.

panels.title: Indexes still to build
panels.description: How many of the indexes taken down for the initial copy are not built yet. The target answers queries more slowly without them, so this should reach 0 not long after the copy.

panels.title: Building now
panels.description: The index being built right now, and the stage its build is at: reading the table, sorting, writing the index, then reading the table a second time to pick up rows written meanwhile. Shows nothing when no build is running.

panels.title: Current stage progress
panels.description: How far the build in flight is through its current stage. Sorting and waiting stages report no progress and read 0%.

panels.title: Source up
panels.description: replicare_source_up — is the source database reachable by the controller? DOWN if any selected sync's source is unreachable.

panels.title: Source DB size (whole)
panels.description: replicare_source_db_bytes — on-disk size of the WHOLE source database (Postgres pg_database_size / MySQL information_schema). Includes replicare's capture schema + delta bloat and any unreplicated tables, so it usually exceeds the target.

panels.title: Source replicated size
panels.description: replicare_source_replicated_bytes — on-disk size of JUST the replicated tables (heap+indexes+TOAST). The apples-to-apples comparison with the target's replicated size.

panels.title: Source size over time
panels.description: Whole-database size vs replicated-tables size on the source. The gap is replicare's capture schema + delta bloat + any unreplicated tables.

panels.title: Targets up
panels.description: replicare_target_up — are the replication targets reachable? DOWN if any selected target is unreachable.

panels.title: Target DB size (whole)
panels.description: replicare_target_db_bytes — on-disk size of the WHOLE target database. The state store, when co-located, is a SEPARATE database and is not counted here.

panels.title: Target replicated size
panels.description: replicare_target_replicated_bytes — on-disk size of JUST the replicated tables. On a caught-up sync this converges with the source's replicated size even when the whole-DB sizes differ.

panels.title: Target size over time
panels.description: Whole-database vs replicated-tables size on the target. Watch replicated size converge toward the source's replicated size during backfill.

panels.title: Max replication lag (SLO)
panels.description: Worst per-table replication lag across the selection. Green < 30s, amber < 5m, red beyond.

panels.title: Catch-up ETA
panels.description: How long until the target has applied every waiting change, worked out by replicare from the backlog and how fast it has shrunk over the last 10 minutes. 'Caught up' means nothing has been waiting longer than a minute. 'Not catching up' means the backlog is flat or growing, or the target is unreachable.

panels.title: Inflow vs drain (rows/s)
panels.description: Drain = apply throughput. Inflow ≈ throughput + d(backlog)/dt (the rate deltas are arriving). Inflow above drain means the backlog is growing.

panels.title: Replication lag (per table)
panels.description: replicare_replication_lag_seconds per table — age of the oldest un-applied change.

panels.title: Total delta backlog (rows)
panels.description: sum of unconsumed delta rows across the selection — the whole queue still to apply.

panels.title: Replication lag (per component)
panels.description: Worst lag within each FK connected component (CLAUDE.md §8.1) — the unit of ordering/parallelism. Use it to see which component is behind.

panels.title: Delta backlog (per component)
panels.description: Unconsumed delta rows summed per FK component.

panels.title: Delta backlog rows (per table)
panels.description: Unconsumed delta rows per table. Spikes on churn, drains toward 0 — the catch-up view.

panels.title: Oldest unconsumed delta age (per table)
panels.description: Age of the oldest un-applied change per table.

panels.title: Delta backlog bytes (per table)
panels.description: Estimated unconsumed delta bytes per table — the source-footprint signal.

panels.title: Throughput (rows/s)
panels.description: replicare_throughput_rows_per_second per sync.

panels.title: Apply batch latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile of replicare_apply_batch_seconds over 5m.

panels.title: Error rate (per category)
panels.description: rate(replicare_errors_total) by category (e.g. drain, retention). Should be flat at 0.

panels.title: Delta purge rate (per table)
panels.description: rate(replicare_delta_purged_total) — consumed deltas being reclaimed.

panels.title: Reseeds (selected range)
panels.description: Forced reseeds triggered by the retention cap over the dashboard range. Non-zero = a laggard target was sacrificed to protect the source.

panels.title: Delta purge time (per table)
panels.description: How long each table's last purge of applied changes took on the source, in seconds. It runs on every streaming pass, so it should stay well under a second; each purge statement gives up after 30 seconds. A climbing line means the purge is loading a source we may not own.

panels.title: Leftover track rows cleared (per table)
panels.description: replicare_track_leftovers_removed_total - how many track rows left behind by versions before 0.7.0 the background clean-up has removed from each table since the daemon started. A table appears once its first leftovers are removed and its line then stays flat at its total; a source that never ran an older version shows nothing. (A rate would read 0 here: the clean-up usually clears a table in one round, so its count appears already at its total.)
